PullRequest.Title: Agents - improve brach picker rendering
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request implements the following changes to enhance the branch picker functionality:

- **Default Branch Remote Display**: The branch picker now shows the remote of the default branch (e.g., `origin/main`) when a topic branch is selected. This change ensures that users can see both the current branch and its remote, as well as the default branch and its remote.
  
- **Branch Picker Result Limit**: The previously defined `BRANCH_PICKER_RESULT_LIMIT` has been removed. Instead, the branch pickers now display all branches, but the dropdown height is capped at 10 visible items to maintain usability.

- **Code Adjustments**:
  - Updated the agent host to return the default branch's remote alongside local branches.
  - Adjusted the client cache to ensure it handles branch lists correctly across isolation modes.
  - Modified tests to reflect the new behavior of the branch picker and ensure all branches are accounted for.

- **Documentation**: Help text has been updated to reflect the new behavior of the branch picker.

These changes aim to improve the user experience by providing clearer visibility of branch information and ensuring the branch picker remains manageable in size.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The uncapped helper calls, inherited accessibility callbacks, and scroll-to-row-insertion path are directly traced. The workbench accessibility override returns an empty object for this noncombined picker, so it does not replace the expensive callbacks. Duration and prevalence of very large local-branch collections are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Full-list and prefix array scans and allocations performed by per-row accessibility callbacks.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N matching local branches and k newly rendered rows, getSetSize alone performs O(k*N) work and allocates k arrays of N references; getPosInSet adds prefix copies and scans. Traversing the whole list produces O(N^2) aggregate work. Only roughly ten rows are resident, but N remains the full result count.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased UI-thread CPU and allocation/GC pressure while opening and scrolling large branch lists, risking dropped frames.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The workbench picker passed at most 25 matching branches to ActionListWidget, bounding each accessibility scan and allocation to 25 entries. The separate Agents desktop picker already explicitly requested unlimited results and is not newly affected by this cap removal.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The workbench branch picker supplies an unbounded branch collection to an action list whose accessibility callbacks scan and allocate from the entire collection for every newly rendered row. The new ten-row height cap limits DOM residency, not these callbacks' input size.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: agentHostBranchPicker.ts:14 changes the default limit from 25 to Infinity. AgentHostChatInputPicker._showPicker (agentHostChatInputPicker.ts:898-900) and its filter delegate (:948) invoke this helper without an explicit limit, so the workbench action list now receives all N matching local branches instead of at most 25.
Findings.Title: Precompute row accessibility counts before uncapping branches
Findings.Impact: In repositories accumulating thousands of local branches, opening or scrolling the workbench branch picker repeatedly scans and allocates large branch arrays on the UI thread, creating CPU/GC pressure and potential scrolling jank despite displaying only ten rows.
Findings.Evidence: ActionListWidget's default getSetSize filters _visibleMenuItems for each row, and getPosInSet slices and filters the prefix (src/vs/platform/actionWidget/browser/actionList.ts, accessibilityProvider in the List constructor). ListView.onScroll calls render; render inserts newly visible rows; insertItemInDOM calls updateItemInDOM, which invokes both callbacks at listView.ts:1080-1081. getModePermissionsPickerAccessibilityProvider(false) returns {}. maxVisibleItems only caps height; it does not truncate _visibleMenuItems.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the full branch list, but make accessibility counts constant-time per row: compute action count and prefix positions when filtered items change, or supply equivalent O(1) callbacks for the workbench branch-only list. Refresh those counts on each filter/rebuild.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, filter, and scroll the workbench Agent Host branch picker in a repository with many local branches.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening waits for one branch-completions response, then constructs action items and synchronously initializes/layouts the action list. Filtering uses the captured branch list locally. Scrolling synchronously inserts newly visible rows and computes their accessibility attributes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: connection.sessionConfigCompletions fetches the complete local branch list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per opening; zero additional requests for branch-filter keystrokes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already fetched the full list once per opening and filtered locally; only subsequent UI results were capped at 25.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The picker cannot open until the response arrives.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read local refs with for-each-ref, current branch, origin/HEAD, and verify the default remote ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally four Git processes per uncached completions request, not per branch. Dangling origin/HEAD can add local-ref verification; detached HEAD can add current-commit fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical Git probes and full-list enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Three probes start concurrently; default-ref validation follows its symbolic-ref read. Their results precede the response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return N local-branch value/label records over the existing connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(N) response bytes once per opening; no per-branch RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already serialized all N branches before the client-side 25-result cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of completing the initial response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan/filter the entire list for aria-setsize and copy/filter its prefix for aria-posinset on each newly rendered row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(k*N) full-list work for k rendered rows, plus prefix scans; traversing all N rows gives O(N^2) aggregate work. Approximately ten rows remain resident.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These existing callbacks operated on at most 25 workbench branch results; the diff removes that bound.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously on opening and scrolling, on the UI thread.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct matching local branches, potentially thousands in long-lived repositories, and k rows entering the viewport. No remote-branch enumeration; the selected missing branch adds at most one record.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One completions request per open; backend branch probes use Promise.all with dependent default-ref validation. UI scans and row insertion are serialized on the main thread; cancellation cannot interrupt synchronous scans.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workbench completions are retained for one open picker and reused for all its filter requests; reopening requests them again. The action-list accessibility counts are not cached. Positive, empty, and failed completion responses do not create per-row boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: uncapped helper calls, inherited callbacks, and ListView scroll/insertion calls are directly traced; the branch picker does not override these callbacks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measurements of branch prevalence or frame duration; severity reflects the large-local-branch trigger rather than invented timings.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one materially amplified repeated-work regression: the height cap does not bound per-row full-list accessibility scans.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and search the Agents desktop branch picker or mobile repository bottom sheet in folder/worktree isolation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Wait for cached or initial branch completions, construct picker items, and show the dropdown/sheet. Desktop filtering remaps the local results and pinned groups; mobile maps at most 25 matching branch results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load host-owned branch completions for the draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached promise per draft/workspace, potentially preloaded; subsequent opens, searches, and isolation toggles reuse it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same per-draft promise cache and completions request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold opening awaits the result; a warm opening does not perform another RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate all local refs and read current/default branches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally four Git subprocesses for the single cold draft request, independent of N; the same dangling/detached fallbacks as the workbench path apply.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same subprocess count and full local-branch enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the cold completion response; absent on warm cached opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the full branch completion response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(N) bytes once per draft cache load; neither desktop nor mobile result limits reduce this existing response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already returned the full local branch collection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N cached distinct local branches; at most four current/default pinned branches in worktree mode and two local pins in folder mode, deduplicated by name. Mobile maintains the explicit 25-result limit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One shared load promise per draft. Filtering is local and immediate for branch data. Pin extraction performs a constant number of scans; remaining group-title assignment is one linear pass. The virtual dropdown caps resident rows and uses a fixed width for collections of at least 50 items.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: NewSession._branchLoad caches the successful, empty, or rejected promise for the draft, unchanged by the PR. Label maps retain only the currently bound session's labels. Desktop already passed Infinity before this PR; mobile's previous default 25 limit is now explicit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged cold/warm request cardinality and preserved mobile cap; grouping and deduplication are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Linear item/group allocations increase somewhat with branch count, but no new per-branch external calls or unbounded historical cache growth were established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: desktop results were already unlimited, mobile stays capped, and added grouping is bounded linear work rather than the newly uncapped workbench mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh session Git state after watched filesystem changes, session attachment/restoration, or source-control operations; propagate default-branch metadata to workspace and catalog.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the session's base branch, discover the repository root if needed, await initial Git probes and dependent probes, then update state/persist changed metadata. Background attach/file-watch triggers are off the initial UI critical path; explicit refresh callers await completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run status, remote -v, origin/HEAD symbolic-ref, and default remote show-ref verification; retain existing optional push-remote/divergence probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally adds one show-ref per refresh when origin/HEAD names an origin branch, plus one symbolic-ref when a configured base previously skipped it. Independent session keys refresh separately; repository-root discovery adds one process on a cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: symbolic-ref was skipped for configured bases, and no default-remote verification ran in this method; status/remotes and optional divergence/push probes already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial probes run in parallel; show-ref is in the dependent Promise.all stage and must complete before state publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted diff base when needed and write changed Git metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Optional base metadata read per eligible refresh; one state write when Git state changes, with per-session sequencing for folder maps. Creating drafts skip persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same database operations and change comparison; stored payload now includes two optional branch-name strings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads precede Git computation; persistence precedes completion of refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize existing state updates/catalog metadata with default branch fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two additional optional strings per changed state, not a branch-list payload or per-branch message stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same state serialization and projection boundaries without the two fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing persistence/update paths; catalog propagation does not issue new Git/network probes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of interested session/source keys, not branch count. The file monitor groups watchers by root but fans refresh requests out to eligible sessions; each session throttles computation to at most one refresh per five-second interval under sustained events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ThrottlerByKey coalesces per source/session and includes a five-second delay; there is no new global limiter. Within each computation, initial probes and dependent probes run in separate parallel stages. Session/folder persistence retains existing sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository roots have a 100-entry positive LRU and per-directory discovery sequencing; failures are not cached. Session default-branch probes themselves are uncached. State equality avoids writes when unchanged. Existing GitHub association only runs on branch changes, not solely default metadata changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for added probe count, cache boundaries, watcher grouping, and throttled scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Additional local process cost is real but unmeasured; no new per-branch process fan-out, network access, or additional polling loop was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: Added fixed-count probes implement the requested default-ref metadata/validation. No further high-confidence avoidable scaling regression was established; metadata pass-through alone was not treated as a finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: A folder draft follows an external checkout, or the user toggles folder/worktree isolation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On an actual reported branch change, validate that the folder draft is out of sync, wait for any existing configuration resolution, recheck relevance, optimistically set its branch, and resolve configuration. Config-dependent picker interactions wait while resolving; the state-update handler itself launches this asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the draft's configuration against the host after a relevant external branch change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one request per applied branch change per out-of-sync folder draft. Initial reports, unchanged branches, worktree drafts, already-synchronized picker checkouts, and superseded queued branches are skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: External checkout metadata did not initiate this configuration request; isolation toggles already resolved configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced on the state-update path, off the synchronous handler but on configuration readiness; isolation toggles already awaited this resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read HEAD/current/default branch to authoritatively contribute isolation configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For a normal folder repository, four reads: HEAD rev-parse, current branch, origin/HEAD symbolic-ref, default-ref show-ref. Root discovery adds one only on a miss. Concurrent callers for the same working directory share the pending Git-info read. Worktree resolution additionally reads the current branch ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same host helper/probes existed, but external branch state updates did not call them through configuration resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequential Git-info reads must complete before the resolve response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send existing config values and return the finite schema/value result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small configuration payload per normal resolved branch transition, not all branches or all history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These payloads were exchanged on creation and user config changes, not on external branch reports.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual observed checkout transitions and out-of-sync folder drafts, not all session-state updates or repository branches. Obsolete intermediate transitions are discarded after waiting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each draft waits for its current resolution and rechecks the authoritative current branch/config before starting work. The tests demonstrate A/B/C reports while A resolves produce requests for A and C only. Different drafts may resolve concurrently, with same-directory Git-info reads shared when overlapping.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No settled Git-info cache: overlapping reads coalesce by working-directory key, then the entry is removed. Repository roots remain cached. Existing branch-completion promises are reused rather than reloaded. Copilot, Claude, and Codex resolveChatConfig implementations perform local schema/value processing without SDK/network model enumeration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: request guards, latest-branch recheck, tests, pure provider config resolvers, and pending Git-info coalescing were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote connection latency and draft multiplicity vary; no redundant per-update request or new network/model-discovery fan-out was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the added authoritative resolve is restricted to real out-of-sync branch changes and coalesces obsolete reports. Isolation toggles preserve their existing boundary count.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 20 changed files and every diff page. Traced branch data loading, rendering/scrolling, desktop/mobile isolation behavior, Git refresh scheduling/persistence, and external-checkout config synchronization. Submitted one high-confidence materially amplified UI repeated-work finding. No concrete removed performance regression qualified for internal fix provenance reporting.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
